title: B2 First for Schools Sample Paper 2

partner.name: Hannah
partner.persona: A 17-year-old student from Oxford preparing for B2 First for Schools. Speaks natural British English, thinks aloud briefly when weighing options, and enjoys building on the other candidate's ideas.

1.opening: First we'd like to know something about you.

questions.text: Who are you most like in your family? Tell us about them.
questions.topic: who you are most like in your family

questions.text: Do you have a best friend?
followups: What do you like about them?

questions.text: Who do you spend time with after school?
questions.topic: who you spend time with after school

questions.text: Tell us about a good teacher you've had.
questions.topic: a good teacher you have had

questions.text: What's your favourite subject at school?

followups: What do you like to read?

questions.text: Do you enjoy using the internet in your free time?
questions.topic: using the internet in your free time

questions.text: Tell us about the things you like doing at the weekend.
questions.topic: things you like doing at the weekend

questions.text: Are there any nice places to go in your area?
questions.topic: nice places to go in your area

questions.text: Have you been anywhere nice recently?
questions.topic: somewhere nice you have been recently

questions.text: Where would you like to go for your next holiday?
followups: Why would you like to go there?
questions.topic: where you would like to go for your next holiday

2.opening: In this part of the test, I'm going to give each of you two photographs. I'd like you to talk about your photographs on your own for about a minute, and also to answer a question about your partner's photographs.

task1.title: Ways of learning
photo_descriptions: four students sitting around a table discussing a newspaper article and taking notes together
younger school pupils working individually at desktop computers in an IT room
task1.intro: {candidate}, it's your turn first. Here are your photographs. They show students learning in different ways.
task1.prompt: I'd like you to compare the photographs, and say what might be good for the students about learning in these ways.
task1.card_question: What might be good for the students about learning in these ways?
task1.compare_followup: Which way of learning do you think helps students remember information better?
task1.followup_to_partner: {partner}, do you prefer learning things on your own or with friends? Why?

task2.title: A day out
photo_descriptions: two teenage friends walking along a path in the grounds of a historic stone castle
two friends carrying shopping bags along a town centre pavement
task2.intro: Now, {partner}, here are your photographs. They show friends having a day out together.
task2.prompt: I'd like you to compare the photographs, and say what the friends are enjoying about their day out.
task2.card_question: What are the friends enjoying about their day out?
task2.partner_monologue: Both photographs show two friends spending the day together, though they are doing very different activities. In the first photo, the girls are walking outside near an old castle, so they are probably enjoying the fresh air, the scenery and learning a bit of history. In the second picture, the two friends have been shopping in town and are carrying several bags. They seem happy to have found things they liked and to be chatting together in a lively place.
task2.followup_to_user: {candidate}, which of these things would you prefer to do on a day out? Why?
task2.topic: what you would prefer to do on a day out

3.title: School trip
3.card_question: Is it a good idea for students to go on school trips?
3.opening: Now, I'd like you to talk about something together for about two minutes. Here are some reasons why many students go on school trips and a question for you to discuss. First you have some time to look at the task.
3.start_discussion: Now, talk to each other about whether it's a good idea for students to go on school trips.
3.decision_prompt: Thank you. Now you have about a minute to decide which two things are the most important for teachers to think about when they organise school trips for their students.
3.topic: whether school trips are a good idea for students

questions.text: Do you think school trips should take place on a school day or at the weekend?
questions.topic: whether school trips should be on a school day or at the weekend

questions.text: If you go on a school trip, is it better to visit a city, or go to the countryside?
questions.topic: visiting a city versus the countryside on a school trip

questions.text: What can students do in class after going on a school trip?
questions.topic: what students can do in class after a school trip

questions.text: What's a good place for students to visit in your country?
questions.topic: a good place for students to visit in your country

questions.text: What's the most interesting thing about visiting other countries?
If you could go anywhere in the world, where would you go?
questions.topic: where you would go anywhere in the world

4.closing: Thank you. That is the end of the test.
